steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Media language refers to the ways in which media products communicate meaning to audiences through visual, audio, written, and technical codes. | Key Fact: Denotation is the literal or surface meaning of a sign (what you see). Connotation is the deeper or associated meaning (what it suggests). For example, a red rose denotes a flower but connotes love and romance. | Key Fact: Technical codes include camerawork (close-up, wide shot, low angle), editing (cross-cutting, montage, pace), sound (diegetic, non-diegetic, sound bridge), and mise-en-scene (setting, costume, lighting, props). | Key Fact: Symbolic codes convey meaning through objects, colours, and visual elements that carry cultural significance — e.g. a wedding ring symbolises commitment, dark lighting connotes danger.
